title: Java Collections: choosing the right collection
description: Understand the core collection interfaces and select the right data structure for common interview problems.
content:
## The collection hierarchy

The Java Collections Framework provides interfaces such as List, Set, Queue, and Map. List preserves order and allows duplicates. Set enforces uniqueness. Queue models processing order, while Map associates keys with values.

## Choosing a collection

Use ArrayList for indexed access and iteration. LinkedList can be useful for frequent operations at both ends, but ArrayDeque is usually a better queue or stack. HashSet and HashMap provide average constant-time lookup when hashCode and equals are implemented consistently. Choose TreeSet or TreeMap when sorted order is required.

## Interview checkpoint

Explain the ordering, uniqueness, and lookup requirements before selecting a collection. Include expected time complexity and any thread-safety requirements in your answer.
author: Tech Interview Hub

title: Building REST endpoints with Spring Boot
description: Review controller responsibilities, request mapping, validation, and response status codes.
content:
## Controller fundamentals

A Spring MVC controller maps HTTP requests to application behavior. Use @RestController for JSON APIs and map resources with annotations such as @GetMapping and @PostMapping.

## Keep responsibilities clear

Controllers should validate request shape, delegate business rules to a service, and return suitable HTTP responses. Use request DTOs rather than binding persistence entities directly. Add Bean Validation constraints and handle errors consistently.

## Interview checkpoint

Be ready to explain why POST creates a resource, why PUT replaces a resource, and when PATCH is appropriate. Return 201 Created for a successful creation and include a Location header when practical.
author: Tech Interview Hub

title: Kubernetes readiness and liveness probes
description: Learn how probes help Kubernetes route traffic and recover unhealthy containers.
content:
## Readiness

A readiness probe indicates whether a container is ready to receive traffic. When it fails, Kubernetes removes the Pod from matching Service endpoints while leaving the container running.

## Liveness

A liveness probe detects a container that cannot make progress. Repeated failures cause the container to restart. Avoid making a liveness check depend on a temporary external service, which could trigger unnecessary restart loops.

## Startup probes

A startup probe gives slow-starting applications time to initialize before liveness and readiness checks begin. Configure thresholds and periods based on real application startup behavior.
author: Tech Interview Hub

title: Java exception handling and custom exceptions
description: Choose checked and unchecked exceptions appropriately and preserve useful error context.
content:
## Checked and unchecked exceptions

Checked exceptions must be declared or handled, while RuntimeException and its subclasses are unchecked. Use checked exceptions when callers can reasonably recover and are expected to account for the failure. Use unchecked exceptions for programming errors or failures that callers cannot meaningfully handle at that level.

## Preserve context

When translating an exception at an application boundary, keep the original cause so logs retain the underlying failure. Avoid catching broad exceptions only to return a success-shaped value or silently ignore the problem.

## Custom exceptions

Use a domain-specific exception when it makes an expected failure clearer to the caller, such as AccountNotFoundException. Keep exception names and messages useful, but do not place secrets or sensitive user data in messages that may be logged.
author: Tech Interview Hub

title: Spring Security: authentication and request authorization
description: Separate authentication from authorization and apply least-privilege access to Spring APIs.
content:
## Authentication versus authorization

Authentication establishes who is making a request. Authorization decides whether that identity may perform a particular action on a resource. A valid login alone should not grant every application permission.

## Protect request routes

Configure security rules so public endpoints are explicitly identified and protected routes require an authenticated principal and the appropriate authority. Prefer denying access by default over leaving new endpoints unintentionally public.

## Check access at the resource boundary

For sensitive operations, enforce authorization on the server and consider method-level checks for business actions. Client-side route guards and hidden controls improve user experience but are not a security boundary. Test both unauthenticated and insufficiently privileged requests.
author: Tech Interview Hub

title: Designing clear service boundaries in microservices
description: Use business capabilities and data ownership to define services that can evolve independently.
content:
## Start with business capabilities

A service boundary should reflect a cohesive business capability, not simply a technical layer or database table. Group behavior and the data it owns together so the service can enforce its rules consistently.

## Make ownership explicit

Each service should be the source of truth for its data. Other services interact through stable APIs or events rather than directly changing its database. This reduces hidden coupling and allows internal schemas to evolve.

## Avoid premature splitting

A distributed boundary adds network failures, operational overhead, and consistency challenges. Start with a modular design and split a service when independent scaling, deployment, ownership, or fault isolation provides a concrete benefit.
author: Tech Interview Hub

title: Understanding the Hibernate entity lifecycle
description: Learn the transient, managed, detached, and removed entity states.
content:
## Entity states

A transient entity is a newly created Java object not associated with a persistence context. A managed entity is tracked by an EntityManager or Session, and changes can be synchronized during flush. A detached entity has an identity but is no longer tracked by that context. A removed entity is scheduled for deletion.

## Dirty checking

Hibernate detects changes to managed entities and can generate SQL during flush without an explicit update call. This behavior applies only while the entity is managed and within the persistence context.

## Work with detached data carefully

When updating from an API request, avoid blindly merging client-supplied entities. Load the managed entity, validate the requested changes, and update allowed fields to avoid overwriting data the client should not control.
author: Tech Interview Hub

title: Using MySQL joins and aggregation safely
description: Combine related rows, group results, and avoid common aggregate-query mistakes.
content:
## Join related data

An INNER JOIN returns rows that match in both inputs. A LEFT JOIN preserves every row from the left input and returns nulls for missing right-side matches. Put conditions in ON when they define a match; a filter on the right-side table in WHERE may remove null-extended rows and effectively change a LEFT JOIN into an inner filter.

## Group and aggregate

GROUP BY produces one result per group, and aggregate functions such as COUNT and SUM calculate values for each group. Use HAVING to filter groups after aggregation; use WHERE to filter input rows before grouping.

## Verify query behavior

Check whether joins multiply rows before summing values, add indexes to frequently joined or filtered columns where appropriate, and inspect the execution plan with EXPLAIN.
author: Tech Interview Hub

title: Reading PostgreSQL query plans with EXPLAIN
description: Use query plans and measured row counts to investigate slow PostgreSQL queries.
content:
## Inspect the plan

EXPLAIN shows the plan PostgreSQL expects to use, including scans, joins, estimated costs, and estimated row counts. EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the statement and reports actual timing and row counts, which can reveal where estimates differ from reality.

## Compare estimates and actuals

Large differences may indicate stale statistics, correlated data, or a query shape the planner cannot estimate well. Review the most expensive nodes and the number of rows processed rather than assuming an index scan is always faster than a sequential scan.

## Use care with write statements

EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the query. For a statement that changes data, test in a safe transaction or on representative non-production data and roll back when appropriate.
author: Tech Interview Hub

title: Oracle analytic functions for ranking and running totals
description: Use analytic functions to calculate rankings and aggregates without collapsing result rows.
content:
## Analytic function structure

An analytic function uses an OVER clause with optional PARTITION BY and ORDER BY clauses. Unlike GROUP BY, it can calculate a value across a set of related rows while keeping each input row in the output.

## Ranking examples

ROW_NUMBER assigns a unique sequence within each partition. RANK gives ties the same rank and leaves gaps afterward, while DENSE_RANK gives ties the same rank without gaps. Use a deterministic tie-breaker in ORDER BY when the result must be repeatable.

## Running totals

SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY transaction_time, id) can calculate a running total for each account. Choose the window frame intentionally, especially when rows share the same ordering value.
author: Tech Interview Hub

title: Docker container networking fundamentals
description: Connect containers with Docker networks and understand service-name discovery.
content:
## User-defined bridge networks

Containers attached to the same user-defined bridge network can communicate using their container or service names. Docker provides DNS-based discovery on these networks, which is generally more reliable than hard-coding container IP addresses.

## Publish ports deliberately

A container port is not automatically exposed to the host. Publish only the ports that need to be reachable from outside the Docker network, and bind to a specific host interface when broad exposure is not desired.

## Keep network boundaries clear

Separate unrelated services into appropriate networks and avoid assuming that a published port is private. Review firewall rules and the application's own authentication and authorization independently of Docker networking.
author: Tech Interview Hub

title: Managing application configuration with Kubernetes ConfigMaps
description: Separate non-sensitive configuration from container images and understand update behavior.
content:
## Store non-sensitive settings

A ConfigMap stores non-confidential key-value configuration separately from an application image. Pods can consume its values as environment variables, command arguments, or mounted files.

## Understand when changes take effect

Environment variables are set when a container starts, so changing a ConfigMap does not update a running process's environment. Mounted ConfigMap files may update eventually, but the application must be able to reload them. A rollout restart is a common way to ensure Pods use updated configuration.

## Keep secrets separate

Do not put credentials or tokens in a ConfigMap. Use a Secret with appropriate access controls, and remember that default base64 encoding is not encryption.
author: Tech Interview Hub

title: Using IAM roles instead of long-lived AWS access keys
description: Give applications temporary credentials through IAM roles and reduce key-management risk.
content:
## Prefer temporary credentials

Applications running on AWS can obtain temporary credentials through an attached IAM role rather than storing long-lived access keys. The AWS SDK credential provider chain can retrieve and refresh these credentials automatically in supported environments.

## Apply least privilege

Attach policies that grant only the actions and resources the workload needs. Use separate roles for different applications or environments, and avoid sharing a powerful role across unrelated systems.

## Review identity access

Audit role trust policies, permissions, and usage. Never commit access keys to source control or bake them into container images; rotate and revoke any exposed credentials promptly.
author: Tech Interview Hub

title: Deploying a stateless service to Google Cloud Run
description: Package an HTTP service in a container and configure Cloud Run for scalable requests.
content:
## Prepare the service

Cloud Run runs a container that serves HTTP requests and listens on the port provided by the runtime environment. Build a reproducible image, keep the process in the foreground, and handle termination signals so the service can shut down cleanly.

## Design for stateless instances

Instances can scale out or stop at any time. Store durable state in managed storage rather than the container's local filesystem, and make request handling safe when traffic reaches different instances.

## Configure access and scaling

Choose whether the service is public or requires authentication, grant the runtime service account only the permissions it needs, and set concurrency and scaling limits based on load tests and downstream capacity.
author: Tech Interview Hub

title: Protecting Angular routes with route guards
description: Use functional guards for navigation while keeping the server as the authorization boundary.
content:
## Functional guards

Angular functional guards can decide whether navigation may continue, redirect to another route, or wait for an asynchronous result. They are useful for checking session state and improving the navigation experience.

## Handle permissions clearly

A guard can read route metadata to determine which permission is needed and return a UrlTree when the current user should be redirected. Prefer a single, consistent authorization helper over duplicating permission checks across routes.

## Protect APIs too

A route guard runs in the browser and can be bypassed by a user who controls that browser. Every protected backend endpoint must independently authenticate the request and verify permissions before returning or changing data.
author: Tech Interview Hub

title: Managing subscriptions and cleanup with React useEffect
description: Synchronize a component with external systems and clean up before effects are replaced.
content:
## Effects and synchronization

useEffect is intended for synchronizing a component with an external system, such as a browser event listener, timer, or network connection. It is not required for every calculation that can be derived directly while rendering.

## Return a cleanup function

An effect can return a cleanup function to remove listeners, clear timers, or cancel supported work. React runs cleanup before the effect is set up again with changed dependencies and when the component unmounts.

## Keep dependencies accurate

Include reactive values used by the effect. Missing dependencies can cause stale values, while unstable objects or functions can cause repeated runs. Simplify the effect or stabilize the inputs when repeated setup is not intended.
author: Tech Interview Hub

title: Building reliable quality gates in a CI pipeline
description: Use repeatable builds, automated checks, and clear release evidence to reduce deployment risk.
content:
## Validate every change

A useful CI pipeline checks out a specific revision, restores dependencies reproducibly, compiles the application, and runs appropriate tests and static checks. Failures should be visible and tied to the change that introduced them.

## Promote one artifact

Build an immutable artifact once and promote that same artifact through environments. Rebuilding separately for production can produce different outputs and makes release verification less reliable.

## Keep secrets and approvals safe

Provide credentials through the CI platform's protected secret mechanism, scope them to the smallest required job, and avoid printing them. Add human approval where policy or risk requires it, and keep a rollback path for failed releases.
author: Tech Interview Hub
